title: This Hasn’t Happened Since 2006!
creator: BWB - Business With Brian
summary: Brian (Business With Brian) argues US profits are growing faster than higher interest rates can pull prices down — the first time this setup has appeared since 2006 — even though the 10-year yield is at its highest since 2002 and the week's fall was much rougher under the surface: the S&P 500 slipped about 1% while chip stocks fell about 9%. Since June, expected S&P profits are up about 10% against prices up about 3.5%, and 72 companies guided above forecasts, the most since FactSet tracking began in 2006. He filters for five AI hardware names down more than 9% in the week whose profits are expected to grow at least 15% next year with forecasts raised since July, warning they swing two to three times harder than the market on rate-spike days, so positions should be staged and the riskiest kept extremely small. Vertiv (garbled as 'Verdive' in auto-captions) is the worked example: EPS up about 60%, outlook raised, stock down about 31% since July. All five calls are CONDITIONAL_BUY, each conditional on waiting for imminent earnings and then dollar-cost averaging small: VRT (signal 'buy a lot'; wait for 28 October earnings), NVT, ONTO, FIX and INOD (the riskiest, very small only). VRT softens his prior BUY; NVT, ONTO, FIX and INOD are first tracked.

calls.thesis: Vertiv: signal ladder 'buy a lot', system agrees, PEG ~1, profits expected +36% next year and forecasts raised since July despite stock -31% since mid-July. Condition: wait until after Oct 28 earnings, then DCA in a little at a time, keep position small while trend has not turned. Softens his prior BUY.
calls.base_case: Analyst forecasts raised since July; EPS +60% last quarter, full-year outlook raised.
calls.bull_case: New 2027 Nvidia rack power design lines Vertiv up for an upgrade cycle; gear due end of this year.
calls.bear_case: Sales light last quarter on delayed giant projects; pricey acquisitions; most rate-sensitive name on the list.

calls.thesis: nVent: signal 'buy a lot' stepped down by his system to BUY (still expensive vs own history). Sales +53% last quarter, data-centre gear >$2B expected this year, profits expected +27% next year, forecasts +14% since July while stock -9%. Condition: sit tight until after end-of-month earnings, then maybe start a small position. First tracked BWB call on NVT.
calls.base_case: Forecasts raised ~14% since July; stock ~9% below 50-day, just above 200-day.
calls.bull_case: Data centres now ~60% of business vs 12% at spin-out; cannot build fast enough.
calls.bear_case: Competition — Schneider Electric won cooling slot in AMD's new AI rack design; $1.75B acquisition debt at >6% interest.

calls.thesis: Onto Innovation: price fallen just below bottom rung of signal ladder — no buying until full re-review, which it passes (record sales +35%, backlog >$1B first time, PEG ~0.6, profits expected +44% next year). Condition: let early-November earnings pass first, then keep small and DCA on the way down. First tracked BWB call on ONTO.
calls.base_case: Forecasts raised ~18% since July (10 raises, 0 cuts in last month) while stock -26% since July.
calls.bull_case: Advanced packaging inspection segment expected +80% this year; new long-term targets due Dec 17.
calls.bear_case: Big memory-maker exposure; Chinese memory design news hit the group; a >$200M order rests on a single customer; swings ~3x market.

calls.thesis: Comfort Systems USA: signal 'buy a lot' dialled back by his system to 'buy a little' (priced near top of own range, PEG ~1.3). Sales +50% and EPS nearly doubled last quarter, backlog ~$14B (+73% YoY), profits expected +23% next year. Condition: wait for earnings in a few days, then build a case. First tracked BWB call on FIX.
calls.base_case: Forecasts raised ~11% since July (7 raises, 0 cuts in last month) while stock -16% since July.
calls.bull_case: Tech/data-centre customers now ~60% of sales vs 43% a year ago; beat estimates 4 quarters in a row.
calls.bear_case: Backlog depends on big-tech build pace; most jobs fixed-price, so labour/material overruns hit profit directly.

calls.thesis: Innodata: price slipped below bottom rung of signal ladder; re-review still checks out but no clear setup now. Record quarter (sales +58%), profits expected +27% next year, stock -15% since July at ~half June peak. Condition: hold off until early-November earnings; only riskiest slice of money, very small, add a little over time. First tracked BWB call on INOD.
calls.base_case: Neutrality vs Scale AI (half-owned by Meta) protects it as rivals shun a competitor-owned vendor.
calls.bull_case: Robot motion-data lab and US government AI testing are potential next growth legs, not yet in numbers.
calls.bear_case: Two big-tech customers = ~71% of sales; CEO changed end-September; up to $300M new stock sale plan caps rallies; 10%+ single-day moves 15 times this year.
